label: ompug defines a fixed hybrid publish order: generate_diagram, use_figma place_section, legend, delete obsolete sections, get_figjam verify, targeted screenshots.
The driver addresses FigJam's root node 0:1 and forbids createPage and notify in its placement scripts, a third independent decision against page-based targeting.
Section placement is idempotent by content hash, returning an existing section tagged with the same diagram and run instead of duplicating it; Flow Mode has no idempotency key.

Counted actions are persisted as pending_action before being returned, leaving an explicitly uncertain action to reconcile with get_figjam or a user question before retry; Flow Mode has no uncertain state.
Deletion is scoped to obsolete sections with known ids, performed in one auditable action, and a failure is recorded rather than retried blindly.
Read-back is quantified at a 60% label ratio with missing labels returned; Flow Mode's exact 8-of-8 is stricter but cannot report which labels are missing.
Screenshots are targeted at mismatched diagrams, or all diagrams only with verify-visual; Flow Mode always requests a visual check even when counts match.
Each action declares which official skills must be loaded before it runs, a second implementation of iteration 1's pre-load rule applied per tool.
Sections use a stable DC prefix, a legend section, per-row palette colours and at least 48px padding; Flow Mode has no naming or legend convention for multi-diagram boards.
Verification compares at most 40 expected labels per diagram, showing the corpus treats read-back as a budgeted operation rather than an unbounded diff.

direction: Adopting the 60% label-ratio threshold into Flow Mode
reason: At nine nodes, partial label coverage is a defect rather than a pass.
